method.history: reconstructed from logs (the public RPC keeps minutes of state, so archive state reads are impossible there)
method.validation: reconstruction compared with state read at the end block
method.timestamps: block headers on a 10,000-block grid, linearly interpolated; oracle times are exact (updatedAt)

validation.scope: vault principals and balances, market local cash, our position (liquidity and range), and the v4 pool tick and active liquidity. NOT validated against chain state: swap volumes, fees and markouts (fees are cross-checked against collected fees in section 3); the Ramses pool is checked separately in its own section.

checks.name: v4 pool active liquidity (replayed from Swap + ModifyLiquidity)

capitalPlacement.note: NVDA and USDG are kept separate; USD values use the oracle price (frozen when the feed is stale). Out-of-range liquidity earns no fees.

uniswapFeesAndVolume.venue: Uniswap v4 NVDA/USDG 0.30% (swappers pay LP fee + a constant protocol fee)
uniswapFeesAndVolume.note: Estimate = sum(LP fee x our active-liquidity share); actual = FeesProcessed gross + uncollected at the end block. Opening/closing fee timing (collected before/after the window) explains part of any gap.

markedAtEndBlock.note: the booked exchange rate only moves at a checkpoint; this is where it would stand if the keeper checkpointed at the end block. Annualised figures extrapolate a 24-day window with a one-way price move and are indicative only.

pNVDA.moneyWeightedNote: no supplier mints/redeems in the window, so the money-weighted return equals the time-weighted return
pNVDA.reserveCutNote: the vault keeps reserveFeeBps of collected fees for the loss reserve; the market keeps its reserve factor of borrow interest

ledger.uncollectedPoolFeesAtStart: NOT_AVAILABLE: no historical state on the public RPC; the start figure is excluded, not zero
ledger.returnStatedAs: simple (non-compounded) return on starting equity; no flows, so TWR = IRR
ledger.annualisationNote: extrapolates a ~24-day window with a one-way price move; indicative only

versusHolding.explanation: hold = keep the starting NVDA and USDG; the difference is fees minus reserve cut plus inventory effects

deltaMatchedBenchmark.definition: benchmark holds, at every sample, the same NVDA quantity as the pair and rebalances at the oracle price without fees. The shortfall is a decomposition of inventory P&L, not an extra cost to subtract again.
deltaMatchedBenchmark.caveat: while the feed is stale the benchmark price is frozen, so session gaps appear when the feed resumes

failedOrEventlessTransactions.note: the nonce counts every transaction the cloud keeper wallet ever sent, reverted ones included, so a difference from the number of transactions that left vault events would be reverted or unrelated sends. Events before the window are excluded from the right-hand count, so the difference is an upper bound on reverted sends inside the window. No explorer is reachable, so their gas cannot be itemised.

waitingActions.reason: waits and simulated reverts never reach the chain; they exist only in the keeper's own JSON log. Persist and ingest that journal to count them (handoff 08 section 7).

liquidityPolicy.settlementSwapsNote: settlement swaps are paused in the live pair config, so idle NVDA is NOT counted as USDG redemption capacity, nor the reverse
liquidityPolicy.reserveNote: a borrowing reserve is a floor for new loans and deployments; it is not guaranteed withdrawal coverage

simulatedFullClaimExit.how: eth_call of withdrawForSide as the market at the end block (no transaction)

redemption.label: simulated exit is observed contract behaviour at the end block; the model value is an estimate

borrowing.note: observed: borrow uses getCash and _prepareFixedLiquidity may unwind the vault synchronously for a shortfall; 6a proposes new borrowing must not depend on an unwind. Margin opens and pending multi-step opens are not included.

ramsesFeesAndVolume.venue: Ramses CL NVDA/USDG (dynamic fee, 50% protocol share)

checks.name: Ramses pool tick after the last swap
Ramses pool sqrtPriceX96 after the last swap

ramsesFeesAndVolume.protocolShareNote: read from slot0 at the end block; no SetFeeProtocol event exists inside the window (the run fails otherwise), so it is constant over it
ramsesFeesAndVolume.lpFeeNote: LP fee = swap fee x (1 - protocol share). Whether that LP share is paid through collect() or through the gauge for staked positions is a fork-test question for handoff 01; this is the economic upper bound, not a proven distributable income.
ramsesFeesAndVolume.rewardNote: RAM is not valued here: without an enforceable distribution mechanism for suppliers its value to them is zero (00 section 3).

operatingCostAssumptions: checkpoint cost $0.5737/day = the larger of the observed average $0.1428 and the hourly cadence the vault requires $0.5737
measured cost per recenter $0.0663, per rebalance $0.0376 (Uniswap vault keeper; used as a proxy for Ramses)

uniswapDilutionRealisedRanges.basis: realised ranges, replayed swaps, our share = liquidity / (others + ours)

weeklyNetAprPctAtReferenceSize.label: each value is one 7-day window, annualised

rollout policy +-1200 / trigger 300.capacitySentence: Uniswap v4 NVDA/USDG 0.30% / rollout policy +-1200 / trigger 300 (50/50 start): in this 24-day window under this replay: one fixed trade stream (our size does not change volume, which biases large sizes down), a simplified single range rather than the contract's exact code path, measured keeper cost, a 20% reserve cut, RAM valued at zero, and net of simply holding the same deposit. The window had a one-way oracle move of -11.6%, which hurts any range position versus holding. It is one window, not a forecast: net return versus holding was below 1% a year at every tested size ($10 to $500k). Gross fees were about 9% a year at the best size (average 55% of capital deployed); best case -31.7% a year at $100,000. At $10 operating cost alone is -2096% a year, and the strategy itself adds -120 points. Weekly sub-windows at $1,000 (each 7 days, annualised) ranged -74% to -18% a year.
